_comment: The one shared material palette for every procedurally generated Machine.
Dieselpunk: 1920s-40s heavy industry. Cast iron, welded steel, olive drab
paint over red-oxide primer, oiled hydraulics, soot and grime. Brass and
copper appear only as small fittings - this is not Victorian steampunk, and
a machine that reads as brass has gone wrong.
Declared here rather than in the generator so that visual consistency is a
fact a test can check: the asset suite asserts that every generated .glb
uses materials from this file and nothing else, and that the numbers match.
base_color is linear RGBA, which is what both Blender's Principled BSDF and
glTF's baseColorFactor take, so the value survives export unchanged.

materials.name: CastIron
materials._use: Machine bodies, frames, heavy castings. The default surface.

materials.name: WeldedSteel
materials._use: Plate panels, brackets, catwalks, bolted flanges.

materials.name: OliveDrab
materials._use: Painted housings and cowlings. The silhouette colour.

materials.name: OxideRed
materials._use: Primer showing through where paint has gone, and inner frames.

materials.name: OiledSteel
materials._use: Hydraulic rams, piston rods, shafts. Wet-looking, not shiny.

materials.name: DullBrass
materials._use: Gauge bezels and small fittings only. Used sparingly on purpose.

materials.name: Soot
materials._use: Chimney mouths, firebox interiors, grime in recesses.

materials.name: HazardYellow
materials._use: Port collars and edge stripes. Reads a port at a glance.
